title: Finite-level comparison for constant Qbar-l cohomology
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $K$ be an algebraically closed field in which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $K$-scheme. Write $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ for the coefficient rings [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. For $n\geq1$ let $F_n=\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z}$ be the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, with the usual quotient transition maps, and use ordinary finite-level etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. On the left below, use ordinary adic cohomology in the following precise sense. Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Put $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $A_X=\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*F_n$ as a sheaf of rings, and $\widehat F=A_X[0]$ in the completed-coefficient module category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Thus $\widehat F$ is the regular rank-one completed integral coefficient object, not an unspecified object having given reductions. For finite $E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the integral full category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Let $1_{\mathbf Q_\ell}$ be the image of $\widehat F$ in $\Dbc(X,\mathbf Q_\ell)$, and let $1=(\mathbf Q_\ell,1_{\mathbf Q_\ell})$ in the pair category $\mathcal P_X=\Dbc(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category, def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Define the notation on the left by
$$H^q_{\mathrm{adic}}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P_X}(1,1[q]).$$
Here integral derived global sections and their degree-$q$ cohomology mean $R\Gamma$ and $H^0(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat F[q])$ from [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]; the equivalence with shifted Hom from the regular unit is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-locally-free-derived-hom]. The notation does not mean cohomology of a discrete constant non-torsion sheaf on the small etale site.

Assume that $H^j(X_{\mathrm{et}},F_n)$ is finite for every $j\geq0$ and $n\geq1$. There are natural $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear isomorphisms, for every $q\geq0$,
$$
H^q_{\mathrm{adic}}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\cong
\left(\varprojlim_{n\geq1}H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},F_n)\right)\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell.
$$
The inverse limit uses the maps induced by $F_{n+1}\to F_n$. These identifications commute with the maps induced by constant sections $\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z\to H^0(X_{\mathrm{et}},F_n)$. The constant-section compatibility means taking the inverse limit of these finite-level maps and then extending scalars, with the constant $1$ corresponding to the identity of $1$.

source.place: Finite-level passage sentence, stated precisely with a finiteness hypothesis. Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 19, pp. 123-125 (integral inverse-limit cohomology); Stacks Tag 07KY, more-algebra-lemma-break-long-exact-sequence (Milnor correction); coefficient realizations compared by the pro-etale formalism.

proof.text: The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ satisfies [lem-cbc-compactification-geometry-fibre-bound]: a field has just the ideals $0,K$, hence is noetherian and has zero-dimensional spectrum. Thus $X$ is noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $\ell$ is invertible on $X$. These are exactly the scheme hypotheses of the integral and finite-stage categories. For every finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ put $S_E=\varprojlim_m(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_X$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. There each finite level, with $P=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, is the sheafification of $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]; sending a scalar to the constant function maps the constant presheaf $U\mapsto P$ to it, compatibly with the quotient maps. This map is locally injective (injective for nonempty $U$; an empty object is covered by the empty family) and locally surjective: an affine open of $U$ is quasi-compact, so a continuous function to the finite discrete $P$ has finitely many open fibres there, on each of which it is constant, and these opens cover $U$. Hence it induces an isomorphism of sheafifications [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] with the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], a ring isomorphism since the presheaf map is. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], $S_E=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, the coefficient sheaf pulled back from the point; at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ this is $A_X$. The regular complex $S_E[0]$ belongs to the integral category by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization](ii): take the single stratum $X$ and the perfect scalar complex $\mathcal O_E[0]$. Its reductions are the regular finite coefficient modules, by $S_E\otimes^L_{S_E}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_X=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_X$. Hence the units used in the statement are actual objects of these categories.

source.place: Finite-level passage: identify the completed constant unit and verify the domain of the coefficient categories; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2(1).

proof.text:
Set $G_n=\nu_X^*F_n$. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] these are the constant pro-etale sheaves with the same finite coefficient rings and the same constant sections. Quotient maps of constant finite sheaves are epimorphic: a section is locally a scalar, and one lifts that scalar through the surjection of rings. Thus [det-pe-continuous-cohomology-limit] gives $A_X\simeq R\varprojlim_nG_n$ and $R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X)\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},G_n)$. For each $n$, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] applies to the finite ring $\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ and the degree-zero complex $F_n\in D^+$; its natural unit comparison identifies the latter tower with $C_n=R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},F_n)$. Equivalently this composite is the comparison stated in [det-pe-continuous-cohomology-etale]. Apply [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] to this countable tower in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, reindexing from $n\geq1$ to $n\geq0$. It gives
$$0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{q-1}(C_n)\to H^q(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X))\to\varprojlim_nH^q(C_n)\to0.$$
These are ordinary finite-level etale groups by [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The right arrow is induced by the coefficient projections, and all comparisons are natural in the tower.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.10, pro-etale continuous-cohomology comparison; Stacks Tag 07KY, more-algebra.tex, lemma-break-long-exact-sequence for the D(Ab) Milnor sequence.

proof.text:
If $q\geq1$, every $H^{q-1}(C_n)$ is finite by the hypothesis. The finite-group clause of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler] gives $R^1\varprojlim_nH^{q-1}(C_n)=0$; no surjectivity on cohomology is required. If $q=0$, $H^{-1}(C_n)=0$ since $F_n$ is in degree zero and ordinary right-derived sections are nonnegative; this zero tower is finite too. Thus in all the stated degrees the projection map of Step 2 is the natural $\mathbf Z_\ell$-linear isomorphism
$$M_q:=H^q(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X))\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_nH^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},F_n).$$
Linearity follows already at each projection from the quotient action $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$.

Module sheaves on the small ringed site form a Grothendieck category by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], hence have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] with $M=S_E$ and $U=X$, the ordinary abelian cohomology used in Steps 2–3 equals the module-valued derived-section cohomology, naturally in all module maps and identically in degree zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-locally-free-derived-hom] on the small pro-etale site with $R=S_E$, $P=S_E$, and the bounded-below complex $K=S_E[0]$. Its dual is $S_E$ by evaluation at $1$, so this gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S_E)}(S_E[0],S_E[0][q])\cong H^q(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},S_E)).$$
The integral category is full by [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], so its Hom group between these objects is exactly this ambient Hom group. At $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ it is $M_q$. In degree zero the identity of the regular module is the section $1$: the evaluation comparison in the cited lemma sends a regular-module endomorphism $u$ to $u(1)$. This fixes the normalization needed for constant sections.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, global Hom formula with the perfect object R[0]. Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, makes the module/abelian comparison explicit.

proof.text:
Choose a $\mathbf Z_\ell$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathcal O_E$ using [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. The basis map of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free] is $A_X^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_E$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i b_i$, using the coefficient identifications of Step 1. Consequently the natural map
$$M_q\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathcal O_E\longrightarrow H^q(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},S_E)),\qquad h\otimes b\longmapsto (a\mapsto ab)_*(h)$$
is an isomorphism: on this basis both sides are $M_q^{\oplus d}$ and the map is the identity on its coordinates. To compute the right side, a finite sum of injective resolutions is again an injective resolution (extend a map to a finite tuple by extending each coordinate); sections and cohomology take that finite sum to the finite sum. This also computes cohomology on the underlying abelian sheaves: restriction of $S_E$-injectives to $A_X$-modules preserves injectives since its left adjoint, tensor with the finite free $S_E$, is exact. The map is independent of the chosen basis since its displayed formula does not use a basis. For an inclusion $E\subset F$ it sends $h\otimes b$ along both comparison paths to the class induced by $a\mapsto ab$ in $S_F$. Thus these isomorphisms commute with coefficient inclusions.

source.place: Basis-induced finite direct-sum identification, applied to ordinary derived sections; the displayed bilinear map makes the comparison canonical.

proof.text:
The scalar-extension functor of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] sends $1_{\mathbf Q_\ell}$ to the rational image $1_E$ of $S_E[0]$. Indeed, its integral functor is tensor with the completed coefficient sheaf, and multiplication gives $A_X\otimes^L_{A_X}S_E\cong S_E$; shifts are respected by its specified shift comparisons. Now use the Hom-localization formula in [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] itself:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dbc(X,E)}(1_E,1_E[q])
&=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)}(S_E[0],S_E[0][q])\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\\
&\cong (M_q\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathcal O_E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E
\cong M_q\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}E.
\end{aligned}$$
Here the first comparison is Steps 4–5, and the last is balancing, $(h\otimes b)\otimes e\mapsto h\otimes be$. The definition is raw localization of Hom groups; it requires neither a field-extension lemma for $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathbf Q_\ell$ nor an additional identification with an ambient category of localized sheaves. At $E\subset F$, the scalar-extension, associator and shift maps in the pair-category definition send these classes by $h\otimes e\mapsto h\otimes e$ with $e$ viewed in $F$: Step 5 checks this before localization, and tensor balancing checks it afterwards.

source.place: Finite-level passage, rationalization and scalar extension of the unit; Milne Section 19, p. 126; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), realized here by the defining Hom localization.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] and [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category],
$$H^q_{\mathrm{adic}}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)=\varinjlim_E\operatorname{Hom}_{\Dbc(X,E)}(1_E,1_E[q])\cong\varinjlim_E(M_q\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}E).$$
This colimit is $M_q\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Explicitly the map sends $[E,\sum_i h_i\otimes e_i]$ to $\sum_i h_i\otimes e_i$. Every element of the latter tensor product uses finitely many algebraic scalars, hence is represented over a single finite field $E$. Every equality of such tensors follows from finitely many additive and balancing relations; their scalars also lie in a single finite overfield, so the map is injective. Existence of that overfield is the compositum property in [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. The scalar action agrees with that in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] by enlarging the field to contain the acting scalar. Substitute the integral isomorphism of Step 3 to obtain exactly the displayed isomorphism of the item, in every $q\geq0$.

source.place: Finite-level passage, passage from finite coefficient fields to the common Qbar-l stage; elementary tensor relations in the defining directed colimit.

proof.text: For constant sections, the map $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X)$ sends $a=(a_n)_n$ to the compatible constant sections $(a_n)_n$. Projection to $G_n$ gives its constant scalar $a_n$; the comparison of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] carries this to the same scalar section of $F_n$. Hence Step 3 takes $a\cdot1$ to $(a_n\cdot1)_n$ under the inverse limit of the maps in the statement. The normalization in Step 4 identifies $1$ with the identity of the regular unit. The maps of Steps 5–6 carry that identity to the identity of $1_E$ and send $a\otimes e$ to its scalar multiple; the colimit and scalar action in Step 7 then give the claimed constant-section compatibility after tensoring. For a scheme morphism $u:Y\to X$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) identifies the inverse images of the completed coefficient rings with the corresponding coefficient rings on $Y$. For finite coefficients the two composite inverse images through the etale and pro-etale sites agree by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The composition and naturality clauses (4) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] therefore identify the two induced cohomology maps, including maps to each finite quotient. The natural limit comparison [det-pe-continuous-cohomology-etale] then commutes with these projections. The bilinear maps of Step 5 commute with pullback since $a\mapsto ab$ pulls back to the same coefficient map; the scalar-extension and shift coherences of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] carry this equality through localization and the pair-category colimit. This proves the asserted naturality as well as the constant-section clause.

source.place: Constant-section compatibility and naturality of the finite-level passage.
